keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Baol row). The page: a strip of land extending east from the ocean, with Touba, Diourbel and Mbacké, south of Cayor and north of Sine, with the seaports of Saly Portudal and Mbour. "Baol regained its independence in 1756." The union with Cayor under the Damel-Teigne is drawn in the cayor dossier, so Baol has no shape from 1549 to 1755 here; the page also has Lat Sukaabe Fall conquer Cayor "in 1697".

ledger.note: The Damel-Teigne union: Amary Ngoné Sobel Fall "became the first Damel-Teign, reigning over both kingdoms in a personal union". The page gives no year for the union and its ruler list has him at c. 1560-1593; the cayor dossier has the gain in 1549 (confidence 2) and this entry follows it. The union is a personal union, not an annexation, but the shape is drawn under Cayor until 1756.

notes:
Baol, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Baol (one page).

The 1549-1755 personal union with Cayor is recorded as a loss here (confidence 1, year from the Cayor page) and drawn in the cayor dossier; this keeps the two dossiers consistent and leaves Baol without a shape for two centuries. If the viewer should show Baol as a distinct kingdom in the union, the keyframe baol_1549 (Diourbel, 1549-1755) can be added. The page's own statements disagree on the 1550s: "Around the turn of the 16th century" Cayor invaded Baol, and Amary Ngoné's reign is c. 1560-1593. The Baol-Cayor conquest year of Lat Sukaabe Fall is 1697 here and 1693 on the Cayor page. The Baol page has no month for the 1894 end. The Mbour and Saly coast is not drawn (the gazetteer region is Diourbel only).
Gazetteer: Lambaye, Touba, Mbacké, Mbour, Saly Portudal.
